name: Suntera Denim Trucker
description:
A four-pocket denim jacket in the classic trucker silhouette — fitted through the chest and shoulders, cropped at the hip, with the signature yoke seaming across the back. Suntera sources a medium-weight indigo denim that fades beautifully and unevenly with wear, so after six months every jacket looks different from every other. Button front, button cuffs, two chest pockets with button flaps, two side entry pockets.

Suntera is a mid-tier street label out of the corridor's Pilsen district. They don't sell in corponation retail chains — only in independent shops and direct. The Trucker is their flagship piece and comes in raw indigo, a pre-faded light wash, and a deep black dye that turns greenish-grey over time. People who wear Suntera tend to know about Suntera. People who don't wear it sometimes resent the people who do.
what_it_says: You have opinions about clothes without making it your whole personality. You know what's good without needing anyone to tell you.
worn_by: Tier 2 and Tier 3 people with taste
anyone who buys from independent labels
story_hooks: Suntera's founder has been approached to collaborate with a Tier 4 corponation label — the independent shops that carry Suntera are watching carefully, and some have said they'll drop the brand if it happens.
A limited run of Suntera Truckers was produced with a small hidden embroidery on the interior yoke — a symbol that means something to a specific underground community.
Someone is selling convincing Suntera counterfeits in the Shelf markets; the quality is almost as good as the real thing, which raises questions about where the materials are coming from.
